scope: Additional nominal SQL restoration in two fresh databases inside the existing local RESTORE stack. Existing original databases, Auth identities, roles, credentials and HTTP services remain unchanged.

coordination.targetDatabases: Two new UUID names, never postgres; source schema/ACL and only existing two identities/profiles and one existing group/membership are cloned by the lifecycle owner.
coordination.destructiveOperations: No DROP, reset, --clean, server reconfiguration, new role, new credential, new identity, or original-table write. Retain both databases and private dumps for the final retention owner.

nominalFixture.openingBalances: Both accounts start at zero. The twenty ordinary economic ledger rows establish the balances; no hidden opening adjustments are excluded from the count.
nominalFixture.transactions: Income A10000 + income B2000 + eight income/expense pairs A100 each + transfer A→B100 + transfer B→A100 = exactly20 rows. Two transfers preserve total12000. Income12800, expense800, net12000.
nominalFixture.lots: Three distinct manual USD lots in investment account A:1×100,2×50,4×25; current units110,55,27.5. Exact cost300, current330, unrealized30USD, realized0. Registration is an external purchase reference and creates no cash-ledger row.
nominalFixture.rule: One owned inactive daily expense rule1000 with last date05Oct. No cron/provider call is made.
nominalFixture.group: Exactly one existing cloned synthetic group and its existing members/capability; no new guest or external credential.
nominalFixture.postSnapshotLoss: After the private dump, insert one owned expense1500 dated06Oct11Z into only the nominal source. Source becomes21rows and A8500/B2000; restored snapshot must retain20rows and A10000/B2000 and omit the exact lost-row UUID. Record its reconciliation separately; do not reapply it.

timeEvidence.boundaries: RPO86400 and RTO14400 inclusive pass;86401 or14401 fail. These are explicit contract calculations, not observed wall-clock durations or a23-hour-old operational backup.
timeEvidence.actual: Record real UTC backup/restore/validation timestamps and monotonic durations independently. Never wait or alter the OS clock merely to produce the nominal3h30 number.

assertions: Lifecycle confirms source cloned only permitted metadata and target literally empty before restore; original RESTORE postgres fingerprints stay identical.
Before dump exact IDs/counts and numeric manifest2accounts/20transactions/3lots/1rule/1group match the independent equations.
pg_dump custom archive has private0600 path, SHA256 and TOC; source snapshot stays unchanged during dump.
pg_restore --exit-on-error targets only the new empty database; all public/auth/storage table hashes and schema/functions/grants/RLS/index catalog match the dump snapshot.

Restored Auth users/identities are the same existing two. SQL SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated with A/B claim fixtures demonstrates row isolation and no privileged-role bypass; this is not normal HTTP Auth login.

Four CU SQL read oracles agree with the restored ledger/accounts/analysis/lots; transfer UPDATE/DELETE and investment sale can be tested inside rollback-only transactions, followed by identical full data hashes.
Any Storage metadata/binary fixture is declared explicitly; SQL catalog alone is not Storage API acceptance. Existing independent-stack Auth/Storage/UI evidence is cited separately.
remainingBlockers: No observed backup entitlement/mechanism of the actual contracted deployment plan.
The nominal23h/3h30 and boundary times are a fixture model, not an observed end-to-end RPO/RTO service outage.
GoTrue/PostgREST/Storage HTTP stay bound to the original database; no four-CU UI journey on these additional nominal databases is claimed.
The unresolved Arc window/JS state remains a separate browser blocker; this plan opens no browser.
